newsitem.title: USA: CME March feeders limit up, live cattle higher.
newsitem.headline: CME March feeders limit up, live cattle higher.

text.p: CME March feeder cattle posted limit gains of 1.50 cents per lb in late trading, with the market continuing to attract buying in reaction to lower CBOT corn futures and higher cattle and hog markets, traders said.

Limit gains in CME hogs and pork bellies provided early support to the cattle markets, as did lower CBOT corn futures. Strong gains in live cattle fueled additional buying in feeder cattle to carry those contracts sharply higher to limit up.
A major reason for Monday's hog gains was the USDA hog report, which showed four percent fewer hogs as of December 1 than a year ago and showed farmers were not rebuilding herds.

At 1227 CST, feeder cattle were up 1.500 to 1.250 cent with March up the limit at 68.550, which also is a contract high. Live cattle were up 0.1.000 to 0.550 cent with February 1997 up the most at 65.800.
